candidates.title: Due-date reminders from a spreadsheet

demandEvidence.chore: Connect Google Sheets to a Make scenario using Search Rows to automate reminders based on spreadsheet due dates.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I want to connect Google Sheets to my Make scenario using the Search Rows module so I can automate reminders based on due dates stored in a spreadsheet.

ease.reason: The request names Sheets, Make and Search Rows, enough to scope a test; the source gives no setup instructions or implementation reference.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: a small consultancy might pay to reduce missed due-date follow-ups; one forum request does not establish payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test can use operator-supplied synthetic rows and a reminder output; live account access and delivery reliability remain unresolved.

autonomy.reason: A scheduled search could identify due rows, but the discussion provides no supported implementation and a person should verify reminders and failures.

evidence.reason: The fresh request states a concrete spreadsheet reminder chore, but not recurrence, constraints, successful implementation or paid demand.

candidates.reason: Concrete task supports a bounded synthetic-data reminder experiment. No supplied implementation reference supports the mechanics; provisional mean is below 6, so this is excluded.

candidates.title: Log AI-agent runs in a sheet

demandEvidence.chore: Record each agent run's name, task ID, status and time in a Google Sheet when it finishes or fails.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Every time an agent finishes or fails a task, Make should record the agent name, task ID, status and time in a Google Sheet.

ease.reason: The post specifies four fields and a Sheets destination for a test; no supplied building reference documents the integration mechanics.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: automation consultants maintaining client agent workflows might pay for run records; the request proves neither customers nor payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week prototype can accept synthetic completion events and append the named fields to a test sheet; production access and event reliability are unproved.

autonomy.reason: A proposed event-to-row loop is bounded, but no supplied reference proves it works and a person must inspect missing or incorrect records.

evidence.reason: The post gives a specific run-recording task and fields, but no measured recurrence, implementation proof or paid demand.

candidates.reason: The chore is concrete enough for a proposed synthetic-event experiment, but implementation support is absent and the provisional mean is below 6. It also risks overlapping the AI-agent operations customer in recent posts, so it is not proposed.

rejected.title: AI output policy evaluation
rejected.reason: The excerpt describes a product evaluating AI outputs against schemas and business rules; it does not state an external user's chore or request. The maker's product description is not demand evidence for a separate service.

rejected.title: HN Sieve Show HN listing
rejected.reason: The only supplied text is a Show HN title announcing an AI scoring and summarizing product. It gives no distinct user's chore; a listing title alone cannot support an experiment.

rejected.title: ZeGrapher research graphs
rejected.reason: The excerpt expresses a feature wish for graphs usable in research articles but does not identify a concrete user's input-to-output task or recurring workflow. No implementation reference is attached to bound a useful experiment.

rejected.title: Steam Frame wireless setup
rejected.reason: The excerpt says the maker built a tool to set up a hidden wireless access point on Linux. It is a product description, not a distinct public request or manual chore to automate.

rejected.title: Due-date reminders from a spreadsheet
rejected.reason: Assessed above: provisional five-criterion mean is 5.4, below threshold 6; no supplied implementation evidence supports the proposed mechanics.

rejected.title: Log AI-agent runs in a sheet
rejected.reason: Assessed above: provisional five-criterion mean is 5.4, below threshold 6; no supplied implementation evidence supports the proposed mechanics, and recent AI-agent operations posts create customer overlap risk.

rejected.title: Beginner workflow automation guidance
rejected.reason: The literal text only says the poster is new and seeks guidance. It names no concrete chore, so a service task or experiment would have to be invented.

steps.message: Assessed all seven sealed discussion assignments. Two posts specify concrete spreadsheet chores and received provisional five-criterion assessments; both are below the 6 threshold, with no matching supplied implementation references. The other five lack a supported bounded chore or are product descriptions. No post proposed.
